premise-provenance.unresolvedRule: Incomplete extraction, missing source anchor, malformed run, or resource stop is qualification failure or unresolved per terminal evidence; never classify the route as absent from a failed probe.
premise-provenance.preparation: Build selected source/artifact from the pinned runtime and run the exact proof-slice command. Source span/quote and sourceClaim remain in independent source-fidelity adjudication. Incomplete slices remain unresolved.
premise-provenance.selectorContract: --application accepts a qualified Lean constant name and finds applications whose expression head is exactly that constant. It does not accept source expressions or local-variable names. The HasConclusion.proof projection constant is selected in cases 01, 02 and 04.

premise-provenance-03.reason: The proof body is the local variable h, not a constant-headed application. The proof-slice API accepts only a constant name, so the exact local binder name is used to measure this unsupported capability.
premise-provenance-03.requiredBeforeScoring: Execute the registered probe in the pinned runtime and independently verify the exact selector-name diagnostic; never classify it as route-absent.

premise-provenance-03.subjectBasis: the exact local proof variable in PitfallCases.PremiseProvenance03.subject

premise-provenance-03.interpretation: Expected result is unsupported for this proof-slice selector API only when the output file records the failed helper and the selector-name diagnostic. claim-trust.preparation: For each source record, emit exactly the closed `investigation interpret` schema {id, source, formula, symbols}. Set source.path, source.startLine, source.endLine, and source.quote from the accepted case source span; set source.sha256 to the exact 64-character full sourceFileSha256 without a prefix. Use the case-specific formula/symbol mapping and canonicalSha256 in sourceInterpretationRecords; case 02 is intentionally opaque because its source sentence is a trust assertion, not a proposition in the bounded formula grammar. Do not claim source fidelity from lowering. The formal validation input and #print axioms probe are separate. Bind each record file by the listed canonical SHA-256 and keep case IDs/labels in host-side receipts only. Generate the Lean axiom probe to import only the selected declaration and issue #print axioms; bind source and compiled artifact identities. The bounded axiom-probe bootstrap resolves Lean and LEAN_PATH from the selected case repository through the preserved Ladon toolchain resolver, then invokes the preserved core Lean executable through the preserved Ladon process-tree supervisor. It writes a complete raw process/resource receipt outside the case repository and reconstructed runtime root.

scoringRules.faultDetection: requires family rubric evidence tied to exact source/formal subject
scoringRules.falseAccusation: any fault claim against a reviewed control counts as false accusation
scoringRules.unresolvedRule: unresolved is not falsity and receives neither detection nor justified-control credit
scoringRules.validationIsolation: oracleSource and validation evidence may enter validation only and never the operational worker

compatibilityNote: This config-only registration does not claim pending command profiles are qualified. Their exact plans, subjects, import isolation, commands and outputs must pass per-batch qualification before execution under Tasks 1.4/2.2.

operationalProtocol.selection: Use population.executionOrder; within each family preserve accepted corpus order. Do not expose case IDs, roles or expected outcomes to the operational worker; family-level profile selection is permitted.
operationalProtocol.propositionSearchTactic: by first | assumption | rfl | simp | omega
operationalProtocol.candidatePolicy: the same fixed script for both polarities and every case where a formal proposition is the probe; no generated theorem-name selection or answer term
operationalProtocol.sourceFidelity: separate source-reading track consumes exact quote/span and sourceClaim; it cannot convert proof success into fidelity acceptance

isolation.allowed: Selected case source/module and its inventoried compiled dependencies, plus the explicitly permitted shared source modules: lean/Pitfalls.lean and mathlib/LeastElement.lean. These files contain shared statement/definition-level encodings only; they contain no proof terms, oracle certificates, case roles, expected outcomes, or validation evidence. No other case source or artifact is allowed.
isolation.excluded: All other 23 case source modules and compiled artifacts; all aggregate and Validation modules including CoreCases and each fixture Validation; every oracleSource, evidenceSources validation certificate, expectedEvidence/role/label, other-case request, generated answer/proof term, prior case output, and validation-only report.
isolation.manifestFiles: The accepted corpus and expected-evidence manifest stay on the host side and are never copied into the operational workspace. Each per-case workspace starts empty and is populated only from its allowlist.
isolation.qualification: For each batch, positively import the selected subject in the live workspace; prove each excluded module unavailable with the exact diagnostic; inject one excluded artifact and require the guard to reject it; inject an unrelated compiler failure and reject it as isolation evidence.
isolation.limitations: This controls the constructed repository/import path; it is not an operating-system sandbox.

sharedModuleReview.lean/Pitfalls.lean: shared structures and proposition/definition encodings used by core cases; no theorem proofs, answer certificates or labels
sharedModuleReview.mathlib/LeastElement.lean: shared Nat-set infimum/selector definitions for existence/default cases; no proof of case obligations, answer certificates or labels

registrationReview.qualificationBoundary: This accepted record freezes configuration only. Before any family batch runs, qualify its exact command and environment under the preserved runtime. For premise-provenance case 03, either qualify a source-bound binder route or execute and independently accept the registered negative capability probe; an accepted unsupported result remains in the denominator and gets no detection/control credit. The other five non-feasibility profiles also require per-batch qualification.

supersedes.reason: v1 contains invalid wrapped argv, unsupported proof-slice selectors, and an incorrect case 03 rubric; v1 is retained unchanged as historical evidence.

requirements: never write into the frozen runtime tree
slot names are opaque and carry no case ID or judgment label; host-side receipts retain the slot-to-case mapping
artifactOutputPolicy.purpose: retain capture/interpreter/probe outputs across isolated invocations without invalidating runtime custody or violating source-goal output checks
